pages.title: Bert Rudge
body: So. You're the new manager.
Took a high-school team all the way to the national championship, did you? Very impressive.

pages.title: The books bite
body: This is a REAL professional team. Players earn wages every week, whether they played like champions or garden furniture.
Contracts, facilities and the rest can wait until they matter. For now, keep one eye on the money at the top.

pages.title: Know your doors
body: These are the only doors you need today. I'll explain the machinery behind them when it can actually hurt us.

pages.title: One player. One drill.
body: Choose a player, assign a drill, then run the session. Training costs TP (Training Points) and money, so don't scatter it around because a button looks cheerful.

pages.title: That's your week
body: You're done for this week.
Just remember to check your inbox to know what to do.

inbox.title: Meet the coach market
inbox.detail: Bert has found several adults with whistles and opinions.

pages.title: Pick your football brain
body: The coach market refreshes each pre-season. Better candidates want a bigger club, more fame and, naturally, more money.
Compare level, two specialties and weekly wage. A whistle is not evidence of competence.

inbox.title: Hire your first head coach
inbox.detail: Choose specialties that fit how you want the squad to grow.

pages.title: One chair. Choose well.
body: A head coach boosts matching training and may permanently teach the club a formation or drill.
Their wage arrives every week, including weeks when their clipboard achieves very little.

inbox.title: Make room for an assistant
inbox.detail: A Coaching Office unlocks the second staff slot.

pages.title: Build the Coaching Office
body: The Coaching Office opens an assistant-coach desk. Until then, the second tracksuit has nowhere official to lean.
Place it on the grounds like any facility. The cost lands immediately, and upkeep starts each week.

inbox.title: The assistant desk is open
inbox.detail: Add a second set of specialties—and a second weekly wage.

pages.title: Hire the other assistant
body: An assistant coach adds smaller specialty bonuses beside your head coach. Different strengths give the staff room more reach.
Yes, this technically makes me the assistant to the assistant. I shall survive.

inbox.title: Place your first facility
inbox.detail: Bert has the grounds plan and only one coffee ring on it.

pages.title: Build with a little plan
body: Choose a building, then an empty patch on the 8 by 6 grid. If it fits and we can pay, it opens immediately.
Leave useful neighbours room to share an edge. Future you is an expensive contractor.

inbox.title: Upgrade a facility
inbox.detail: More output and more upkeep, applied immediately.

pages.title: Level up the grounds
body: Select an existing building to see its next level and price. Upgrades apply immediately, up to Level 3.
Check the weekly upkeep before approving it. Shiny tiles have recurring opinions.

inbox.title: You found an adjacency bonus
inbox.detail: Some neighbouring facilities work better as a pair.

pages.title: Edges make bonuses
body: Certain facility pairs earn a bonus when they share an edge. Corners do not count; buildings are fussy like that.
Discovered pairings stay recorded, and you can relocate buildings when the puzzle needs another go.

inbox.title: Send your first scout
inbox.detail: Pick a region and a focus, then let the binoculars work.

pages.title: One mission at a time
body: Choose a region and focus, pay the mission cost, then wait for the due week. A better Scout Office brings clearer reports.
We can send one scout at a time. Apparently they share the club binoculars.

inbox.title: Your scout has reported back
inbox.detail: Open the shortlist before calling any agents.

pages.title: Read the ranges
body: Scout reports reveal a shortlist with estimated stat ranges. Better facilities tighten the guesswork.
A report lets you open transfer talks. It does not make the transfer fee disappear, sadly.

inbox.title: The transfer window is open
inbox.detail: List a player only when the squad—and your heart—can spare them.

pages.title: List, then listen
body: During an open window, list one of your contracted players to invite real bids from other clubs.
A sale brings cash and removes the wage. Bert's rule: count the defenders before selling a defender.

inbox.title: A transfer bid has arrived
inbox.detail: Compare the saved offers; accepting one completes the sale.

pages.title: The bid is the bid
body: Each bidder names an exact fee. Accepting moves the player, credits the cash and clears their wage from our books.
You may also walk away. An envelope is not a court summons, despite the chairman's stationery.

inbox.title: Your first contract negotiation
inbox.detail: The club fee is only half the conversation. Now convince the player.

pages.title: Numbers first. Pitch second.
body: Set wage, term and any promise. You have up to three rounds; an insulting offer can end the call early.
A Pitch Card can sway the effective ask by at most 20 percent. Charm helps. Arithmetic still owns the building.

inbox.title: Youth intake is ready
inbox.detail: Meet this pre-season's academy prospects.

pages.title: The kids have arrived
body: Each pre-season offers one or two young players for a small signing bonus. A better Youth Field improves the crop.
Roster space and future wages still matter. Potential is exciting; payroll remains literate.

inbox.title: Your first National Cup
inbox.detail: Every division enters. One upset can change the season.

pages.title: No table. No second chances.
body: The National Cup mixes clubs from all five divisions in a knockout draw. Win and the next round brings more prize money and fame.
A giant-killing is wonderful. Being the giant is mostly admin and nerves.

inbox.title: Your first injury
inbox.detail: Open the player file and check the repaired Starting XI.

pages.title: Out means out
body: An injured player cannot train or play until the OUT counter reaches zero. The team sheet repairs itself with an eligible replacement.
Review the player and the replacement before match day. The physio has banned my miracle sponge again.
pages.objective: REVIEW THE INJURY AND LINEUP REPAIR.

inbox.title: The emergency loan arrived
inbox.detail: One rescue only. Review repayments and recurring costs.

pages.title: A bridge, not a lifestyle
body: The club received its one automatic emergency loan. Repayments begin next season and this rescue will not repeat.
Cut recurring costs now. The board owns another red folder and far too many pens.
pages.objective: REVIEW THE LOAN AND WEEKLY COSTS.

inbox.title: Your first transfer request
inbox.detail: Low morale has become paperwork. Review the player before selling.

pages.title: They want the door
body: A transfer request comes from sustained low morale. Review their role, contract and the depth behind them before listing anyone.
The request is serious. The dramatic envelope is, regrettably, optional.

inbox.title: A player has announced retirement
inbox.detail: They can finish the season before hanging up the boots.

pages.title: The boots have a date
body: A retirement announcement gives you notice: the player can finish this season, then leaves the active squad.
Use the farewell well. Sentiment is free; replacing their position generally is not.

inbox.title: A club legend leaves a legacy
inbox.detail: Choose a future coach candidate or a mentored youth player.

pages.title: Choose what comes next
body: A long-serving, famous retiree can enter the coach market with a loyalty discount or mentor a special youth player.
One legend, one legacy. Even statues have budget limits.

inbox.title: Urgent: board cash ultimatum
inbox.detail: Reach the cash target within four weeks or the board will force a sale.

pages.title: Four weeks to recover
body: The board has set a cash target and a four-week deadline. Its three or four possible sale candidates are visible now.
Raise cash yourself and the threat clears. Miss it and the board chooses only from that list, at a discount.

inbox.title: Protect one player
inbox.detail: Mark one visible board candidate as untouchable before the deadline.

pages.title: Choose who cannot be sold
body: Protect one player from the board's visible candidate list. You may change your choice while the ultimatum is active.
Your protected player is safe. No hidden names, no surprise sale, no chairman rifling through the whole squad.
